blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 1.16
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 1.16

blocks.text: शुद्धतत्त्वसन्धानाद्वापशुशक्तिः
blocks.directed: [slowly] शुद्धतत्त्वसन्धानाद्वापशुशक्तिः

blocks.text: Śuddhatattvasandhānād vāpaśuśaktiḥ.
blocks.directed: Śuddhatattvasandhānād vāpaśuśaktiḥ.

blocks.text: Through union with the pure principle, the power of bondage associated with the limited being is absent.
blocks.directed: Through union with the pure principle, the power of bondage associated with the limited being is absent.

blocks.text: You Are No Longer a Bound Little Animal.
blocks.directed: You Are No Longer a Bound Little Animal.

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Right.

blocks.text: We have to talk about paśu.
blocks.directed: We have to talk about paśu.

blocks.text: Because in Śaiva terminology, paśu is the bound individual.
blocks.directed: Because in Śaiva terminology, paśu is the bound individual.

blocks.text: Literally, the word can mean animal or beast.
blocks.directed: Literally, the word can mean animal or beast.

blocks.text: But don’t misunderstand this as an insult to animals.
blocks.directed: But don’t misunderstand this as an insult to animals.

blocks.text: It’s a technical designation for the individual limited by the bonds called pāśa.
blocks.directed: It’s a technical designation for the individual limited by the bonds called pāśa.

blocks.text: The paśu experiences itself as separate, incomplete, and constrained.
blocks.directed: The paśu experiences itself as separate, incomplete, and constrained.

blocks.text: And the tradition contrasts this with Pati — the Lord.
blocks.directed: And the tradition contrasts this with Pati — the Lord.

blocks.text: The bound being and the Lord.
blocks.directed: The bound being and the Lord.

blocks.text: Now, if Śiva were fundamentally separate from the individual, you’d have a terrible philosophical problem.
blocks.directed: Now, if Śiva were fundamentally separate from the individual, you’d have a terrible philosophical problem.

blocks.text: How does a finite being ever become truly infinite?
blocks.directed: How does a finite being ever become truly infinite?

blocks.text: How does something inherently limited acquire the nature of the limitless?
blocks.directed: How does something inherently limited acquire the nature of the limitless?

blocks.text: You can’t simply glue infinity onto a finite object.
blocks.directed: You can’t simply glue infinity onto a finite object.

blocks.text: Very messy business.
blocks.directed: Very messy business.

blocks.text: But Trika’s answer is different.
blocks.directed: But Trika’s answer is different.

blocks.text: The limitation is a contraction within the manifestation of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The limitation is a contraction within the manifestation of consciousness.

blocks.text: It is not the ultimate nature of consciousness.
blocks.directed: It is not the ultimate nature of consciousness.

blocks.text: Through śuddhatattvasandhāna, union with the pure principle — identified by Kṣemarāja with Paramaśiva — the binding power no longer governs the yogi’s identity.
blocks.directed: Through śuddhatattvasandhāna, union with the pure principle — identified by Kṣemarāja with Paramaśiva — the binding power no longer governs the yogi’s identity.

blocks.text: And notice the word vā.
blocks.directed: And notice the word vā.

blocks.text: “Or.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Or.”

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja introduces this as another means of understanding the attainment described previously.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja introduces this as another means of understanding the attainment described previously.

blocks.text: The yogi recognises the world as inseparable from the pure reality of Śiva.
blocks.directed: The yogi recognises the world as inseparable from the pure reality of Śiva.

blocks.text: The power of paśutva, bound individuality, is overcome.
blocks.directed: The power of paśutva, bound individuality, is overcome.

blocks.text: In the language of recognition:
blocks.directed: [short pause] In the language of recognition:

blocks.text: You do not turn a fundamentally non-Śiva entity into Śiva.
blocks.directed: You do not turn a fundamentally non-Śiva entity into Śiva.

blocks.text: You recognise that the apparently limited individual was never ultimately separate from Śiva.
blocks.directed: You recognise that the apparently limited individual was never ultimately separate from Śiva.

blocks.text: Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: The chains weren’t another cosmic being’s property.
blocks.directed: The chains weren’t another cosmic being’s property.

blocks.text: They were part of the Lord’s own self-concealment.
blocks.directed: They were part of the Lord’s own self-concealment.

blocks.text: And now the self-concealment is being recognised.
blocks.directed: And now the self-concealment is being recognised.
